fixes.title: The four Session charts are computed over three different frame populations; the guiding chart includes frames the app rejected
fixes.summary: Root cause was that each chart picked its own population: HfrChart filtered isAccepted, the other three filtered nothing, and none filtered frameType. Introduced one canonical population, sessionChartFrames(images) in widgets/session_chart.dart (accepted light frames), removed HfrChart's private filter so no chart can drift again, and made _SessionTab.chartGrid pass that single list to all four charts. The stat strip's acceptedLights helper now delegates to the same function, so the strip and the charts cannot describe different frames. Added a caption above the grid stating the population and how many frames were excluded, so dropping the rejected/calibration frames is disclosed rather than silent.
fixes.test: 'all four session charts plot the same accepted-light frames' in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/session_chart_population_test.dart - renders the Session tab over 2 accepted lights + 1 rejected light (rms 4.2") + 1 dark and asserts every SessionChart holds exactly 2 points and no guiding value above 0.95
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting: with chartGrid passing the unfiltered list and HfrChart's isAccepted filter restored, the test fails with 'Guiding performance plots a different population from the others ... has length of <3>'. Restored and re-ran green together with quick_capture_summary_test.dart. The two analytics capture goldens (captures_landscape_test.dart) fail, but they already failed on this working tree before my change (8.4%/17.6% diff with my caption removed vs 17.1%/23.8% with it) - the master images predate an existing structural change to the screen. Not regenerating them: repo policy is to never commit Linux-regenerated goldens.

fixes.title: Exported FWHM is fabricated from HFR with the wrong factor (2.35x instead of 2x), overstating FWHM by 18%
fixes.summary: Confirmed still present and unfixed. Every site is outside my ownership list (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/{session_export_service,session_report_service,capture_preview_loader}.dart), so I did not edit them. I did land the one piece that IS mine and that the fix needs: ImagesDao.getFwhmForSession(sessionId), a batched read of the MEASURED fwhm column. That column is v50 raw DDL and therefore is NOT a field on the generated CapturedImage data class - a fixer who writes `image.fwhm` will find it does not compile, which is the trap in the finding's proposed fix.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/database/images_dao_session_fwhm_test.dart covers the new DAO method (session scoping, measured-only rows, empty map). No test asserts the corrected export value yet because the exporter is not mine to change.
fixes.caveats: The DAO method is currently uncalled - it exists so the shared change below is three lines instead of a new query.
fixes.needs_shared_change: The physics: HFR is the half-flux RADIUS (native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stats.rs:672), = sqrt(2 ln 2)*sigma = 1.1774*sigma, and FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.000*HFR. The 2.35 factor treats a radius as a sigma and inflates every FWHM by 17.7%. (1) session_export_service.dart exportToCsv: after `final images = await _imagesDao.getImagesForSession(sessionId);` add `final measuredFwhm = await _imagesDao.getFwhmForSession(sessionId);` and replace line 70 with `final fwhm = measuredFwhm[image.id] ?? (image.hfr != null ? image.hfr! * 2.0 : null);`; change the CSV header 'FWHM (px)' to 'FWHM (px, measured or 2x HFR)'. (2) Same in the JSON export at line 171. (3) session_report_service.dart:301 `meanFwhm: meanHfr == null ? null : meanHfr * 2.35` -> `* 2.0` (better: average the measured values from getFwhmForSession and only fall back). (4) capture_preview_loader.dart:178-181 currently OVERWRITES the measured value it was handed - it should be `fwhm: capturedImage.stats.fwhm ?? (capturedImage.stats.hfr != null ? capturedImage.stats.hfr! * 2.0 : null)`; as shipped the live capture readout shows the inflated number during a run.

fixes.title: Insights invents a guiding baseline of 0.1 arcsec when there is no history, so every user with <=5 sessions is told their guiding degraded 7x
fixes.summary: Confirmed still present and unfixed: equipment_health_service.dart:200 takes baseline = recentSessions.skip(5).take(10), which is empty for any user with 5 or fewer sessions; _mean([]) returns 0.0 and the .clamp(0.1, 100.0) at :207/:213 turns 'no data' into a 0.1 arcsec baseline, so recent/0.1 always clears the 1.25x and 1.15x triggers and deducts 18+14 points. The file is a shared service outside my ownership list (it also backs the Equipment screen), so I did not edit it. The Analytics call site (science_analytics_tab.dart:387) is mine, but filtering the insights there would relocate the defect rather than fix it - the invented baseline and the score deduction both happen inside analyze().
fixes.test: None written - the fix belongs in a file I cannot edit, and a test asserting the corrected behaviour would fail on main until that change lands.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/equipment_health_service.dart: make the two baselines nullable instead of clamped. Replace the baselineGuiding/baselineHfr computations (:205-213) with `final baselineGuidingValues = baseline.map((s) => s.avgGuidingRms).whereType<double>().toList(growable: false); final double? baselineGuiding = baselineGuidingValues.isEmpty ? null : _mean(baselineGuidingValues);` and likewise for HFR, then gate the two triggers on `baselineGuiding != null && ...` (:222) and `baselineHfr != null && ...` (:234). No score deduction when there is nothing to compare against. Suggested test in packages/skotiq_core/test/services/equipment_health_service_test.dart: five sessions with avg_guiding_rms 0.65/1.10/0.70/0.55/0.60 and avg_hfr 2.90/4.20/3.00/2.50/2.20 must yield no 'Guiding degradation' and no 'Focus quality drift' insight and an undeducted score; sixteen sessions whose oldest ten genuinely guided better must still raise it.

fixes.title: Stored photometry for a past session is invisible: the light curve is filtered by the CURRENT global target selection
fixes.summary: sessionLightCurveProvider is keyed on (sessionId, objectId) and the Analytics science tab was passing the LIVE selection for objectId in all three places. Reviewing is not capturing: a stored night's rows are keyed on the object that was being tracked then. Added _reviewedPhotometryObjectId (science_analytics_tab/navigation_and_snapshots.dart), which keeps the live selection whenever the session's own rows contain it - so live capture and a user who re-picks the same star behave exactly as before - and otherwise falls back to the object those rows measured most, counting only role='target' rows that carry a differential magnitude so a comparison star can never be promoted into the target's curve. The resolved id now feeds the session light curve, the sessionless/quick-capture curve (same defect shape) and the cross-night campaign curve, so the campaign strip cannot report 'no data' for the star the night below it plots. Also fixed the ladder symptom the finding cites: evaluateLadder now treats lightCurvePoints > 0 as proof the star was tracked, instead of asking a user reviewing a finished night to 'Pick a target' above their own finished curve.
fixes.test: 'a reviewed session plots the photometry it actually recorded' + 'comparison stars are not promoted into a light curve' in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_reviewed_light_curve_test.dart (renders ScienceAnalyticsTab over a stored 20-point V-TEST curve with the live selection defaulted to 'target_primary'); 'a stored curve counts as tracked when nothing is live' in science_ladder_model_test.dart
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting each fix separately: without the resolver the widget test fails with 'Found 0 widgets with text "Differential Photometry"' (i.e. the card is still the 'has no data yet' placeholder), and without the ladder change the ladder test fails with 'Expected RungState.done, Actual RungState.ready'. The write side (science_processing_service) still keys rows on the live selection's objectId; that is correct behaviour and unchanged.

fixes.title: Optical Train Diagnostics grades a session with ZERO data as "A - Excellent"
fixes.summary: The domain model had no way to say 'not measured': a 0.0 penalty is the BEST score, so an empty PSF field map and an empty residual table graded identically to a perfect optical train. Added OpticalTrainDiagnostics.tiltMeasured / collimationMeasured (default true, so no caller had to change) and OpticalHealthScore.isMeasured; letterGrade now renders '-' and qualityLabel 'Not measured' when either axis had no data behind it. tiltMeasured is false when the tiles span a single row AND column (no gradient can exist between one position); collimationMeasured is false unless residuals exist on BOTH sides of the 0.25/0.75 split, because the score is an edge/centre RATIO and the 0.1 clamp otherwise supplies the missing half. The issues list stops claiming 'Optical train looks stable' on unmeasured axes and names what was not measured instead, which also corrects the Analytics Insights panel (science_insights_engine republishes these issues verbatim). dominantTiltDirection reports 'unknown' whenever tilt is unmeasured.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/optical_train_unmeasured_test.dart - 5 cases: empty inputs grade '-' / 'Not measured'; tiles without residuals do not vouch for collimation; edge-only residuals are not a comparison; a single tile is not evidence of a flat field; a genuinely measured balanced field still grades A
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting the service to the old semantics (flags forced true, plain grade labels): 4 of the 5 cases fail; the 5th is the positive control that must pass both ways. Also had to add an edge residual to the existing 'reports stable optics for balanced field' fixture in optical_train_diagnostics_service_test.dart - it asserted the 'balanced across the image' verdict from a single CENTRE sample, i.e. it encoded the defect.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_screen/health_summary_cards.dart and optical_alignment_cards.dart are outside my ownership and still state verdicts from the raw doubles. They should consult the new flags: _HealthGradeCard._gradeColor should use a neutral colour when !diagnostics.healthScore.isMeasured; _ScoreBar should render '-' instead of a 0 bar when the matching axis is unmeasured; _TiltAssessmentCard (line 173+) should replace the 'Within range' badge and 'Score 0.0: tilt looks controlled for this session.' line with 'Not measured' when !diagnostics.tiltMeasured; optical_alignment_cards.dart:195/208 should replace 'Edge/center residual ratio: 0.0' and 'Center and edge behavior look balanced for this session.' when !diagnostics.collimationMeasured. The service change is non-breaking, so those files compile unchanged in the meantime and the headline grade already reads '-' / 'Not measured'.
